_policy: Default-deny. Only tools listed in `allowlist` are registered. RED denylist is enforced at catalog load time (see _hackingtool_deny_pattern in tool_catalog.py).
_review_notes: Starter subset: audit identified ~45 GREEN + ~85 YELLOW tools. This initial catalog lands 12 GREEN + 0 YELLOW to prove the pattern. YELLOW tools require the runtime Shield authorized_scope gate (TICKET-HACKINGTOOL-YELLOW-RUNTIME, deferred). Expanding the GREEN allowlist is a pure data-file change once the runtime gate for YELLOW is in.

red_denylist_reasons.phishing: Credential-stealing kits with near-zero legitimate use outside isolated red-team labs. Accessorial liability exposure for MAS-AI.
red_denylist_reasons.ddos: Stress/flood weapons with no defensive equivalent. Accept raw target URLs with no authorization check.
red_denylist_reasons.payload: AV-evading malware generators (RATs, droppers, silent webcam capture, Android payloads).
red_denylist_reasons.keylogger: Silent keystroke exfiltration. No consented-use path that Daena's governance permits.
red_denylist_reasons.wifi-active: Rogue AP / evil-twin / deauth = active denial-of-service against wireless networks and their users.
red_denylist_reasons.android-abuse: Lockscreen phishing, SMS spam, malicious APKs targeting third-party handsets.
red_denylist_reasons.idn-homograph: Punycode-lookalike URL generator used exclusively for phishing.
red_denylist_reasons.social-bruteforce: Social-network credential brute-forcers. ToS violation + account takeover tool.
red_denylist_reasons.doxxing: Geolocation + social-engineering tools targeting specific individuals without consent.
